svg.title: Proof with a full POVM upper certificate. For arbitrary conclusive effects Ebq with P b Ebq ≤I, the largest eigenvalue of ρbq is [ν + (1 −ν)mq]/(NM). Thus correct probability in that block is at most cq times its conclusive probability. The latter is at most wq because the prior average is Imq/(NM). This proves the linear-program upper bound without assuming a covariant candidate. It is attained by the invariant effects
